subagent_tasks.description: bounded Plans/**/*.md scan for doc discovery / owner-unknown groups

docs_or_topics_assigned: After this merge, the authored top-level `Plans/*.md` surface is fully covered: all `61` docs now have all six requested model passes.
Base route/open primitives landed, but missing:
Cluster D - Route / open-subject / bridge-field refinement misses
Keep Progress widget composition, but bind widgets to canonical runtime and orchestration objects:
No planning-doc edits were made outside the required work-item ledger/meta files; session-local `plan.md` was updated for execution tracking only.
Owner docs must go first, primary stale consumers second, mirrors and checklists after.
Reconcile terminal widgets so targeting uses runtime/worker identity rather than `tier_id` as the primary selector.
Reconcile usage and evidence families away from tier-first cross-surface correlation.
Research Progress - 2026-03-17 - owner-contract seam: Contracts_V0 runtime identity, blocked identity, route/open ownership
Same-file supersession remains a major source of stale implementation guidance.
Still preserves `TierContext`-era live canon rather than fully reflecting `execution_unit_context` direction.
That still makes it dangerous: once upstream reconciliation happens, these docs can continue to broadcast stale “PASS” status or outdated feature summaries unless they are explicitly rechecked.
The `ContractRef` syntax break in `GATE-003` is a hard owner-doc integrity defect, not a style preference.
The `GPT-5.2` continuation wave still produced substantive new deltas across the full 22-doc tail, so the tranche has still not converged before the final `GPT-5.3-Codex` pass.
The blocked/runtime lineage work already moved toward:
The next best stage is condensation so the compact blocker bundle matches the sharper live-doc evidence.
The older request-centric sections are no longer compatible with the later canonical correction sections.
The v2 `canon_inventory.json` keeps only the eight surviving canon clusters needed for the remaining blockers.
The v2 `open_gaps.json` keeps only unresolved blocker families and their exact missing items.
This invocation closes the bounded audit on the three deferred coverage blockers left after doc-discovery resolution (`17` resolved, `3` unresolved).
Treat any remaining `tier_id` use as derived compatibility metadata or view grouping, not as the primary cross-surface key.
`Orchestrator_Page.md` still describes HITL requests as `hitl.*` events keyed by `request_id`
`UI_Command_Catalog.md` contains both the stale graph-HITL command family and the newer canonical `cmd.runtime.*` family in the same file.
`meta.json` remains active; this sweep is still not ready for reconciliation.
`storage-plan.md` is not just a stale consumer. It is still publishing canonical key shapes. Any unresolved tier-era key there will keep propagating into other docs.
`widget.completed_prose` is also still described as completed tier summaries even though evidence and summary records are moving toward stronger object-backed surfaces.
dashboard/current-task language still uses current tier / phase-task-subtask progress bars as if that were the canonical Orchestrator model
deprecated field names such as `allowed_actions[]` must not appear in new canonical schemas
graph detail and usage pivots aligned to node/attempt/runtime identity
historical/current usage navigation aligned to canonical route/open primitives
lane/worktree, receipt, and cross-surface lineage concepts are present
normalization of routed object pivots away from `layout/UI state only`
persistence should be through canonical blocked/runtime records
retire `run.tier_*` event teaching from runtime snapshot guidance
section `6` allows `ContractName:<path>#<anchor>` but section `2` does not follow that same rule
storage-plan still lacks the practical join model from attempt → provider → usage → receipt
the doc title and role model still say `Overseer Protocol` with `Builder`, `Verifier`, and `Overseer` as the primary execution framing
visible labels must bind to the shared runtime recovery commands
worker/verifier identity fields aligned to canonical requested/effective runtime disclosure
